chunks: What the Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, informed me of, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ya'qub ibn Yaqtin, from Abu al-Hasan عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about ghusl (ritual bath) of janabah: is there wudu (ablution) in it or not, according to what Jibra'il عليه السلام brought down? He said: “The person in janabah performs ghusl: he begins by washing his hands up to the elbows before dipping them into the water; then he washes whatever impurity has affected him; then he pours water over his head, his face, and his entire body. Then he has completed the ghusl, and no wudu (ablution) is required of him.”

The Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, said: Every ghusl other than ghusl of janabah is not sufficient for taharah unless the person performs with it the wudu (ablution) of salat (prayer) before the ghusl. What has already preceded contains sufficiency, if Allah the Exalted wills, and what follows will add further clarification.

key_terms.الْجُنُبُ: a person in a state of janabah
key_terms.الْمِرْفَقَيْنِ: the elbows, up to which the hands are washed here
key_terms.غُسْلِ الْجَنَابَةِ: the ritual bath required due to janabah
key_terms.وُضُوءَ الصَّلَاةِ: the ablution specifically performed for salat (prayer)

ai.seo_question: Does ghusl of janabah replace wudu (ablution) in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the procedure of ghusl (ritual bath) for janabah and states that wudu (ablution) is not required along with it. It also notes, in the Shaykh's statement, that other types of ghusl do not suffice for ritual purity without wudu (ablution) for salat (prayer).
